source_text: Persistit sane invehi in nos et adiungit: Hi autem, qui concupiscentiam istam contra evangelicos et apostolicos libros, quos vacuo lectitant, bonum ausi sunt dicere, videas - inquit - sanctos eorum nunc cum filiabus dormisse, nunc cum pluribus et concubinis et uxoribus miscuisse negotium, nec hoc Apostoli vident: " Quae societas luci et tenebris, fideli et infideli, Christo et Belial? " [n236] . Errant glomerati nubilo concupiscentiae, cuius veneno ita fruuntur, ut amentia capti, cum hoc gerunt, a Deo id concessum putent, quasi ignorent Apostolum dixisse: " Quae geruntur ab eis in tenebris, turpe est etiam dicere " [n237] . Vides nempe, quomodo negotium vexat pudoris atque id contra nos valere plurimum putat, qui non malum dicere audeamus, quod velandum tamen pudore fateamur. Nullum vestimentum igitur texuisti, quo deformitatem tui dogmatis operires, praeter pannos, quibus in parentis tui et magistri haereditate crevisti. Persistit igitur erigi in nos faciensque apostrophen: Age tu - inquit - defensor concupiscentiae, aperto sermone narra fructus et opera eius. Ecce ego contra eam non timeo lucem, quam illa trepidat, quam illa odit. " Omnis enim, qui male agit, odit lucem et non venit ad lucem, ne manifestentur opera eius " [n238] . Videsne concupiscentiam mali esse originem, per quam miserae animae libidini serviunt, non sponte, quia hoc est, quod nolente animo gerimus solum [n239] ? Hinc est, quod et tu: Nam quid est - inquis - quod labia, lingua, manus, inflexiones dorsi, cervicis et laterum ut ad opera congrua moveantur, positum in potestate est, cum vero ventum fuerit, ut filii seminentur, membra in hoc opus creata non serviunt, sed exspectatur, ut ea velut sui iuris libido commoveat et aliquando non faciat animo volente, cum aliquando faciat et nolente? Enumerasti tu nempe omnia officia membrorum eaque commendans servire voluntatis imperio libidinis negotium dicis, quod hoc solum animo nolente faciamus. Quid Manichaeus? Videsne - inquit - concupiscentiam mali esse originem, per quam miserae animae libidini serviunt, non sponte, quia hoc est, quod nolente animo gerimus solum? Sed videamus, quid aliud adiungat: Denique omne peccatum extra corpus est, quia actuale est; qui autem fornicatur, in corpus suum peccat [n240] ; omne enim peccatum, antequam fiat, non est et post factum memoria sola eius operis, non ipsa species manet. Malum autem concupiscentiae, quia naturale est, antequam fiat, est, cum fit, augetur, post factum et videtur et permanet. Quid igitur nobiscum iurgas, quia te Manichaeum vocemus, cum nec in illius scriptis aliud, quam quod tu dicis, nec in tuis aliud, quam quod ille vult persuadere, teneatur? Iam vero illud, quod per plebeia, a vobis tamen infusum, ora discurrit, in eadem Manichaei epistula continetur, id est: Si peccatum naturale non est, quare baptizantur infantes, quos nihil per se mali egisse constat? Ideo autem dixi illud per multorum volitare linguas, quia vulgarius argumentum etiam a tardis quibusque comprehensum est. Ceterum tu in libris tuis in eo spem totam reponis; et hoc ergo ipsum hoc modo tuus praeceptor exsequitur: Qui his verbis mihi interrogandi sunt: Si omne malum actuale est, antequam malum quispiam agat, quare accipit purificationem aquae, cum nullum malum egerit per se? Aut si necdum egit et purificandus est, licet eos naturaliter malae stirpis pullulationem ostendere, illos ipsos, quos amentia non sinit intellegere, neque quae dicunt neque de quibus affirmant. Audis, quomodo convitiatur nobis? Amentes vocat nec intellegentes, vel quae dicamus vel quae affirmemus, qui malae stirpis pullulationem negemus, cum baptizemus etiam eos purificante aqua, qui malum nullum egerint, id est parvulos. Posita sunt nempe de eius multa sententiis; sed nisi Menoch filiam et Manichaeum, qui se Christi Apostolum nominat, titulus indicaret, te omnino suum pollicerentur auctorem [n241] . Cum ergo nihil aliud dicas quam quod Mani docente didicisti, putas te in aestimatione Catholicorum aliter habendum quam illum, per quem talium dogmatum sacramenta potasti?
pass_a_gloss: He persists indeed to inveigh against us and adds: But these who have dared to say this desire good against the evangelical and apostolic books, which they read empty, you may see, he says, their saints now to have slept with daughters, now to have mixed business with several both concubines and wives, nor do they see this of the Apostle: What fellowship to light and darkness, to the faithful and unfaithful, to Christ and Belial? They err gathered in the cloud of desire, of whose poison they so enjoy that, captured by madness, when they carry this they think it conceded by God, as if they were ignorant the Apostle had said: What are carried by them in darkness, it is shameful even to say. You see surely how he vexes the business of shame and thinks it avails very much against us, who do not dare to say evil what nevertheless we confess must be veiled by shame. You have therefore woven no garment by which you would cover the deformity of your dogma, besides the rags in which you grew in the inheritance of your parent and teacher. He persists therefore to be raised against us and making an apostrophe: Come you, he says, defender of desire, by open speech narrate its fruits and works. Behold I against it do not fear the light, which that one dreads, which that one hates. For everyone who acts evilly hates the light and does not come to the light, lest his works be manifested. Do you see desire to be the origin of evil, through which miserable souls serve lust, not of their own accord, because this is what we carry with an unwilling mind alone? From here it is that you also: For what is it, you say, that lips, tongue, hands, bendings of the back, of the neck and of the sides, that they be moved to congruent works, has been placed in power, but when it has come that sons be sown, the members created for this work do not serve, but it is awaited that lust as of its own right move them and sometimes does not do with a willing mind, when sometimes it does even with an unwilling? You have enumerated surely all the offices of the members and commending them to serve the command of will you say the business of lust, that this alone we do with an unwilling mind. What the Manichaean? Do you see, he says, desire to be the origin of evil, through which miserable souls serve lust, not of their own accord, because this is what we carry with an unwilling mind alone? But let us see what else he adds: Finally every sin is outside the body, because it is actual; but who fornicates sins into his own body; for every sin, before it is done, is not, and after the deed only the memory of that work, not the species itself, remains. But the evil of desire, because it is natural, before it is done is, when it is done is increased, after the deed both is seen and remains. Why therefore do you quarrel with us, because we call you a Manichaean, when neither in his writings anything other than what you say, nor in yours anything other than what he wants to persuade, is held? Now truly that which runs through plebeian mouths, yet infused by you, is contained in the same letter of the Manichaean, that is: If sin is not natural, why are infants baptized, whom it stands have done nothing of evil through themselves? But I have said that flies through the tongues of many, because a more vulgar argument has been comprehended even by the slow. For the rest you in your books place the whole hope in it; and this itself therefore in this mode your preceptor follows: Who by these words must be asked by me: If every evil is actual, before anyone does evil, why does he receive the purification of water, when he has done no evil through himself? Or if he has not yet done and must be purified, it is permitted to show them a pullulation of an evil stock naturally, those themselves whom madness does not allow to understand either what they say or concerning what they affirm. Do you hear how he insults us? He calls mad and not understanding either what we say or what we affirm, who deny a pullulation of an evil stock, when we baptize even those by purifying water who have done no evil, that is little ones. Many things have surely been placed from his sentences; but unless the title indicated the daughter Menoch and the Manichaean, who names himself Apostle of Christ, they would altogether promise you their author. When therefore you say nothing other than what you have learned with Mani teaching, do you think you in the estimation of Catholics must be had otherwise than him, through whom you have drunk the sacraments of such dogmas?

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS libido; Blaise often sexual desire; Julian treats as created sensation, not a sin-nature
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: He persists in attacking us and adds: ‘As for those who have dared call this desire good against the evangelical and apostolic books, which they read to no purpose, you can see their saints sometimes sleeping with their daughters, sometimes carrying on with several concubines and wives. They do not see the apostle’s question: “What partnership is there between light and darkness, a believer and an unbeliever, Christ and Belial?” (2 Corinthians 6:14–15). They wander wrapped in desire’s cloud, enjoying its poison so much that, seized by madness, when they do this they think God has permitted it. As though they did not know the apostle said: “What they do in darkness is shameful even to mention”’ (Ephesians 5:12).

You surely see how he presses the matter of shame and thinks it tells powerfully against us, because we dare not call evil what we nevertheless acknowledge must be covered through modesty. Thus you have woven no garment to cover your doctrine’s deformity except the rags you accepted in your father and teacher’s inheritance.

He keeps rising up against us and turns directly to his opponent: ‘Come, defender of desire, describe its fruits and works in plain words. See, in opposing it I do not fear the light which it dreads and hates. “Everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds will not be exposed” (John 3:20). Do you see that desire is the source of evil, through which miserable souls serve lust unwillingly, because this is the only thing we do while the mind is unwilling?’

This is the source of your own statement: ‘Why is it that moving the lips, tongue, hands, and the bending of the back, neck, and sides for their proper tasks lies in our power, but when it comes to sowing children, the organs created for this task do not obey? Instead we wait for desire, as though acting under its own authority, to stir them; sometimes it fails to act when the mind is willing, although sometimes it acts when the mind is unwilling’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 1.7). You listed the functions of all the bodily members, emphasized their obedience to the will’s command, and said desire’s activity is the only thing we do against the mind’s will. What does Mani say? ‘Do you see that desire is the source of evil, through which miserable souls serve lust unwillingly, because this is the only thing we do while the mind is unwilling?’

But let us see what else he adds: ‘Every sin is outside the body, because it consists in action; but the fornicator sins against his own body (1 Corinthians 6:18). Every sin does not exist before it is committed, and afterward only the memory of the act remains, not its actual form. But desire’s evil, because it is natural, exists before it is enacted, increases while it is enacted, and afterward both appears and remains.’ Why, then, quarrel with us for calling you a Manichaean, when his writings contain nothing but what you say, and yours nothing but what he wants to persuade us to believe?

And that saying circulating on ordinary people’s lips, though put there by you, is contained in this same letter of Mani: If sin is not natural, why are infants baptized, when they plainly have done no evil themselves? I said it flies over many people’s tongues because it is a more popular argument, understood even by the slowest. In your books, however, you place your entire hope on it. Your teacher develops this very point as follows: ‘I must ask them in these words: If every evil consists in action, why does anyone receive purification by water before doing evil, when he has done no evil personally? Or if he has not yet acted but needs purification, it is possible to show that they are by nature shoots of evil stock—those very people whose madness prevents them from understanding either what they say or what they confidently affirm’ (compare 1 Timothy 1:7).

Do you hear how he insults us? He calls us mad and unable to understand what we say or affirm, because we deny that people are shoots of evil stock, although we baptize in purifying water even those who have done no evil—that is, infants. Many passages from his statements have now been quoted. Yet if the heading did not name his daughter Menoch and Mani, who calls himself Christ’s apostle, they would altogether announce you as their author (see this work 3.172). Since you say nothing except what you learned from Mani’s teaching, do you think catholics should regard you differently from the man through whom you drank in the mysteries of these doctrines?
